Rashi on Gittin 38b:10:1.english: [Does he] require a bill of manumission - [This refers to both] one who consecrates [his slave] and one who renounces ownership [of him]:

Rashi on Gittin 38b:10:2.english: Both this and that - [one who] consecrates [his slave] and [one who] renounces ownership [of his slave]:

Rashi on Gittin 38b:11:1.english: And we raise an objection to our teaching - Against our own teaching:

Rashi on Gittin 38b:11:2.hebrew: אין הגזברין רשאין להוציאן לחירות - ואפי' לקבל מיד העבד פדיונו; דקיימא לן (קידושין כג:): עבד קונה את עצמו בכסף, אם נתנו לו על מנת שאין לרבו רשות בו, פודה בו את עצמו מיד בעליו. והני גזברין אין רשאין לכך, שאין גופן קנוי להקדש, שלא הקדישן אלא לדמן, וזו דרך שחרור הוא ולא דרך מכירה; אבל מוכרין אותן לאחרים והדמים להקדש, ואותן אחרים מוציאין אותם לחירות אם ירצו:
Rashi on Gittin 38b:11:2.english: The [Temple] treasurers are not allowed to emancipate them - [meaning] even to accept his redemption [money] from the slave's hand; for it is established for us (Kiddushin 23b) [that] a slave acquires himself with money: if [others] gave it to him on condition that his master has no claim to it, he redeems himself with it from his master. And these treasurers are not permitted [to do] so, because their persons are not acquired by the Temple treasury, since he only consecrated them for their monetary value, and this is a manner of emancipation and not a manner of sale. However, they sell them to others and the money [goes] to the Temple treasury, and those others may emancipate them if they wish.

Rashi on Gittin 38b:11:3.english: Even he [himself] gives his own value and goes free - [That is,] if he finds someone who will give him money on condition that his master has no right to it:

Rashi on Gittin 38b:11:4.hebrew: מפני שהוא כמוכרו - הגזבר לו לעצמו, כשם שהוא יכול למכור לאחרים, ובלבד שיתנם דרך מקח וממכר ולא דרך פדיון; אלמא המקדיש עבד, קדוש לדמיו:
Rashi on Gittin 38b:11:4.english: Because he is like one who sells him - [i.e.,] the [Temple] treasurer [sells him] to himself, just as he is able to sell [him] to others, provided that [the slave] gives [his value] by way of purchase and sale and not by way of redemption; thus, one who consecrates a slave — [the slave] is consecrated for his monetary value:

Rashi on Gittin 38b:12:1.hebrew: אך כל חרם אשר יחרים איש לה' מכל אשר לו מאדם וגו' אלו עבדיו ושפחותיו הכנענים - שאם הקדישן, מקודשים לבדק הבית; וכיון דיליף טעמא מקרא, קשיא לרב:
Rashi on Gittin 38b:12:1.english: “Notwithstanding, no dedicated thing that a man may dedicate to the Lord from all that he has, of man,” etc. — “these are his Canaanite slaves and maidservants” - [This means] that if one consecrated them, they are consecrated to the Temple treasury; and since [the Tanna] derives [this] rule from a verse, it poses a difficulty for Rav:

Rashi on Gittin 38b:12:2.hebrew: דאמר לדמי - דמיו עלי להקדש, ולא הזכיר עליו שם קדושה:
Rashi on Gittin 38b:12:2.english: Where he said, “For [his] value” - [Meaning, he said:] “His value is [incumbent] upon me [to donate] to the Temple treasury,” and he did not mention a designation of sanctity upon him:

Rashi on Gittin 38b:13:1.hebrew: אי הכי אידך נמי - אמאי אוקמת דפליג אדרב? תרצה נמי דאמר לדמי:
Rashi on Gittin 38b:13:1.english: If so, the other [baraita] also - Why did you establish [it] as disagreeing with Rav? Resolve it also [as a case] where he said "for his monetary value":

Rashi on Gittin 38b:14:1.hebrew: גזברין מאי עבידתייהו - מה רשות יש להן בעבד? הלא אין להן על הבעלים אלא מעות! ואי קשיא: לוקמה כגון דאמר "הרי הוא קדוש לדמיו", דעכשיו הוא קדוש לימכר, ורשותו של גזבר עליו למכור, וכמקדיש קרקע ובהמה טמאה? תריץ: דכיון דשייך בגופו לשון קדושה ד"עם קדוש", כי אמר "הרי הוא קדוש לדמיו", חיילה אגופו למיהוי בן חורין, כדקיי"ל במתפיס תמימים לבדק הבית דאין יוצאין מידי מזבח, בכריתות ובתמורה (דף לג). הלכך, על כרחך מתני' פליגא, למימר דכי אמר "הרי הוא קדוש", לא לשון "עם קדוש" הוי, אלא לשון הקדש לימכר בדמיו:
Rashi on Gittin 38b:14:1.english: What business do the treasurers have - What authority do they have over the slave? Do they not have [a claim] against the owner only for money? And if you ask: Let [the Gemara] establish [the baraita] in a case where he said, "Behold, he is consecrated for his monetary value," so that now he is consecrated to be sold, and [the treasurer's] authority is over him to sell [him], just like one who consecrates land or an unkosher animal? Answer: Since the language of sanctity applies to his person—like [the expression] "a holy people"—when he says, "Behold, he is consecrated for his monetary value," [the sanctity] takes effect upon his person so that he becomes a free man, just as we hold as established law regarding one who dedicates unblemished [animals] for Temple upkeep that they do not leave [the jurisdiction of] the altar, [as taught] in Keritot and in Temurah (folio 33). Therefore, perforce our Mishnah disagrees, saying that when he says, "Behold, he is consecrated," it is not the language of "a holy people," but rather the language of consecration [to the Temple] to be sold for his monetary value:

Rashi on Gittin 38b:16:2.english: And [he] eats - and his handiwork is not consecrated:

Rashi on Gittin 38b:16:3.hebrew: שלא הקדיש אלא דמיו - ולא אמר אלא "הרי הוא הקדש לדמיו", והוי כקרקע ובהמה טמאה:
Rashi on Gittin 38b:16:3.english: As he consecrated only his monetary value - [That is,] he only said, "Behold, he is consecrated for his value," and he is [therefore] like land or an impure animal:

Rashi on Gittin 38b:1:1.english: And they forced her master - because she was fit neither for a slave nor for a free man:

Rashi on Gittin 38b:1:2.hebrew: ואמר רב נחמן - לאו משום דאיתתא מיפקדה אפריה ורביה, אלא מתוך שלא היתה ראויה, לא היתה מיוחדת לאיש, והיו נוהגין בה הפקר בזנות:
Rashi on Gittin 38b:1:2.english: And Rav Nachman said - [They forced her master to free her] not because a woman is obligated in procreation, but rather because since she was not fit [to marry], she was not designated for [any] man, and [people] would treat her as ownerless in licentiousness:

Rashi on Gittin 38b:5:1.hebrew: רשות - משום דכתיב (דברים כ׳:ט״ז) בשבעה אומות "לא תחיה כל נשמה", איצטריך למיכתב "מבני התושבים" "לעולם בהם תעבודו", להתיר אחד משאר אומות הבא על הכנענית שהיא משבעה אומות והוליד בן, שאתה רשאי לקנותו בעבד; והכי מפרש לה בהמקנא:
Rashi on Gittin 38b:5:1.english: Optional - Because it is written (Deuteronomy 20:16) regarding the seven nations, "You shall not let any soul remain alive," it was necessary to write "of the children of the residents" [and] "of them may you take your bondmen forever," to permit [the case of] one from the other nations who cohabits with a Canaanite woman — who is from the seven nations — and fathers a son, [teaching] that you are permitted to acquire him as a slave; and so it is explained in HaMekanei:

Rashi on Gittin 38b:5:2.hebrew: ודלמא ר' אליעזר סבר לה - כר' ישמעאל, ומאי דוחקיה לשנויי לעיל "מצוה שאני":
Rashi on Gittin 38b:5:2.english: But perhaps Rabbi Eliezer holds - like Rabbi Yishmael; and what forced [the Gemara] to answer above, "A mitzvah is different":

Rashi on Gittin 38b:7:1.english: That they emancipate their slaves - And [thereby] they transgress a positive commandment:

Rashi on Gittin 38b:7:2.hebrew: מסיירי נכסייהו - שדותיהם, מסתכלין בשבת לידע מה הן צריכין:
Rashi on Gittin 38b:7:2.english: [That] they inspect their property - [i.e.,] their fields; they look [at them] on Shabbat to know what they need:

Rashi on Gittin 38b:7:3.hebrew: בעידן בי מדרשא - כשהחכם דורש דרשות לרבים בשבת, והם יושבין בסעודה, והיה להם להקדים או לאחר:
Rashi on Gittin 38b:7:3.english: At the time of the study hall - When the sage delivers discourses to the public on Shabbat, and they are sitting at [their] meal, whereas they should have [held it] earlier or later:

Rashi on Gittin 38b:7:4.hebrew: בערב שבת - בלילי שבת, ואין כאן כבוד שבת, דקיימא לן: כבוד יום קודם לכבוד לילה, והם היו מתכוונים בשביל ביטול בית המדרש. ואיכא דמפרשי: בערב שבת ממש, וכן בכל יום מרוב עושר, אבל בהא מיהא איכא איסורא, שיכנס לשבת כשהוא שבע בלא תאוה:
Rashi on Gittin 38b:7:4.english: On the eve of Shabbat - [That is,] on Shabbat night, and there is no honor of Shabbat in this, as we hold [that] the honor of the day takes precedence over the honor of the night, and they intended [this] on account of the interruption of the study hall. And there are those who explain [it as] literally on the eve of Shabbat, and similarly every day, out of great wealth; however, in this [case] at least, there is a prohibition, that he will enter Shabbat when he is sated, without appetite:

Rashi on Gittin 38b:8:1.english: He himself does not become consecrated - for he is fit neither for the altar nor for Temple upkeep:

Rashi on Gittin 38b:8:2.english: For [his] monetary value, he did not say [so] - [For had he meant that,] he should have said, "The monetary value of my slave is [incumbent] upon me":

Rashi on Gittin 38b:8:3.hebrew: דליהוי עם קדוש - ישראל גמור, דכתיב בהו "כי עם קדוש אתה" (דברים י״ד:ב׳); ולא דמי למקדיש בהמה טמאה, דהתם כיון דליכא למימר בה "דתיהוי עם קדוש" קאמר, על כרחך לדמי קאמר, ואע"ג דלא קאמר "דמיה עלי", הכי קאמר: "הרי היא קדושה לימכר"; אבל הכא דשייכא בגופיה לשון קדושה, לא אמרינן לדמי קאמר:
Rashi on Gittin 38b:8:3.english: That he should be a sacred nation - [meaning] a full Jew, as it is written concerning them: "For you are a sacred nation" (Deuteronomy 14:2); and it is not comparable to one who consecrates an impure [non-kosher] animal, for there, since one cannot say regarding it that he meant "it should be a sacred nation," perforce he meant for [its monetary] value — and even though he did not say "its value is upon me," this is what he meant: "behold, it is consecrated to be sold"; whereas here, where the language of sanctity is applicable to [the slave] himself, we do not say [that] he meant for [his monetary] value:

Tosafot on Gittin 38b:11:1.hebrew: אין הגזברין רשאין להוציא אותן לחירות - וכן אמר בפרק הנזקין (לקמן גיטין נב.) גבי יתומין, דאין האפוטרופסין רשאין להוציא אותן לחירות, אבל מוכרין אותן לאחרים כו'. ונראה דהיינו טעמא דאסור דרך שיחרור, דסברי דקא מזלזלי בנכסי יתומים והקדש; אבל דרך מכירה, ידעי כולי עלמא שמוכרין אותן בשויין:
Tosafot on Gittin 38b:11:1.english: The [Temple] treasurers are not permitted to emancipate them - And similarly [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] HaNizakin (later, Gittin 52a) regarding orphans, that the guardians are not permitted to emancipate them, rather they sell them to others, etc. And it seems that this is the reason that it is forbidden by way of emancipation: because [people] think that they are treating the property of orphans and consecrated [property] lightly; whereas by way of sale, everyone knows that they are selling them for their [full] value:

Tosafot on Gittin 38b:8:1.hebrew: גופיה לא קדיש - פי' בקונט' שאינו ראוי למזבח ולא לבד"ה. לדמי לא קאמר — דהיה לו לומר "דמי עבדי עלי". ולא דמי למקדיש בהמה טמאה, דהתם כיון דליכא למימר "למיהוי עם קדוש קאמר", ע"כ לדמי קאמר; אע"ג דלא אמר "דמיה עלי", "הרי היא קדושה לימכר" קאמר. אבל הכא, דשייכא בגופיה לשון קדושה, לא אמרינן דלדמי קאמר. ואם תאמר: ואמאי לא קאמר נמי "קדוש לימכר לא קאמר", כיון דמילתא אחריתא היא? וי"ל כדפירש בקונטרס בסמוך, דאפי' אמר כן בהדיא שיהא קדוש לימכר — יצא לחירות, מידי דהוה אמתפיס תמימים לבדק הבית, דאין יוצאין מידי מזבח לעולם; ולהכי לא מוקי ההיא ד"אין הגזברין" כגון דאמר שיהו קדושין לדמיהן. ומיהו קשה: דאי מדמינן למתפיס תמימים, נימא דאף על פי שהעבד יצא לחירות, צריך לפדייה ויפלו דמיו לבדק הבית, כמו במתפיס תמימים שתימכר לצורכי מזבח, כדאמרי' בהמנחות והנסכים (מנחות קא.): כשהן נפדין, אין נפדין אלא למזבח והדמים הם לבדק הבית, כדאמר בפרק קמא דתמורה (דף ו.) דאף על פי שהוא בלא תעשה, מה שעשה עשוי; ולכאורה משמע ד"ליהוי עם קדוש" קאמר ואינו נותן שום דמים להקדש! ועוד, מאי קפריך מ"אך כל חרם"? דהתם דאמר בלשון חרם, לא שייך לומר ד"למיהוי עם קדוש" קאמר! ועוד, כי משני "דאמר לדמי" — והיינו לפירוש הקונטרס דאמר "דמי עבדי ושפחתי עלי", דאם הקדישם לדמים יצאו לחירות — ואם כן, מאי איריא עבדיו ושפחותיו? אפילו דחברו נמי! ועוד, מאי שנא כנענים? אפילו עבדיו ושפחותיו העברים נמי! ונראה לפרש: "גופיה לא קדיש" — פי' ליאסר בהנאה, כמו בהמה טמאה שמועלין בה, וכן בקרקע אם עקר ממנו חוליא, ואפילו במחובר איסורא מיהא איכא; "לדמי לא קאמר" — שיהא גופיה קדוש לימכר. והשתא פריך שפיר מ"כל חרם", דמיתפסא בהון קדושה ליאסר בהנאה כמו מחרים שאר נכסים; ומשני "דאמר לדמי", שיהיו לימכר, ולא מיירי במקדיש בלשון חרם. והשתא ניחא דדוקא עבדיו ושפחותיו הכנענים. ופריך "אידך נמי דאמר לדמי", ומשני "אי הכי, גזברין מאי עבידתייהו?" — דאותו שהקדישו לדמיו, הוא יפדנו ויהיה שלו:
Tosafot on Gittin 38b:8:1.english: [The slave] himself does not become consecrated - Rashi explained that he is fit neither for the altar nor for the Temple upkeep. "[It is] for [his] monetary value" — he did not say [that], for he should have said, "The value of my slave is upon me." And this is not similar to one who consecrates an unkosher animal, for there, since one cannot say that he meant "to be a sacred nation," perforce he meant [it] for [its] monetary value; even though he did not say, "Its value is upon me," he meant, "Behold, it is consecrated to be sold." But here, where the term "consecration" is applicable to [the slave] himself, we do not say that he meant [it] for [his] monetary value. And if you ask: Why does [the Gemara] not also say, "He did not say [that he should be] consecrated to be sold," since that is a different matter [from saying "the value of my slave is upon me"]? One can answer, as Rashi explained nearby, that even if he said so explicitly — that [the slave] should be consecrated to be sold — he goes free, just like one who consecrates unblemished animals for the Temple upkeep, which never leave the [status of being designated for the] altar. And therefore [the Gemara] does not establish that [baraita] of "the treasurers are not [allowed to emancipate them]" as referring to a case where he said that they should be consecrated for their monetary value. However, this is difficult: for if we compare [it] to one who consecrates unblemished animals [for the Temple upkeep], let us say that even though the slave goes free, he requires redemption and his value goes to the Temple upkeep — just as with one who consecrates unblemished animals, where [the animal] is sold for the needs of the altar, as we say in [the chapter] HaMenachot veHaNesakhim (Menachot 101a): When they are redeemed, they are redeemed only for the altar, and the proceeds go to the Temple upkeep, as [the Gemara] says in the first chapter of Temurah (6a) that even though it is [subject to] a negative commandment, what he did is done! Yet [here], it appears at first glance that he meant "let him be a sacred nation" and he does not give any money to the Temple treasury! Furthermore, what does [the Gemara] ask from "Notwithstanding, no dedicated thing (cherem)"? For there, where he spoke using the term cherem, it is not applicable to say that he meant "to be a sacred nation"! Furthermore, when [the Gemara] answers "where he said [it] for [their] monetary value" — which according to Rashi's explanation means that he said, "The value of my male slave and my female slave is upon me," for if he consecrated them for [their] monetary value they would go free — if so, why specifically "his male slaves and his female slaves"? Even [the value of] his fellow's [slaves] as well! And furthermore, why specifically Canaanite [slaves]? Even his Hebrew male slaves and female slaves as well! Rather, it seems [preferable] to explain: "[The slave] himself does not become consecrated" — meaning, to become forbidden for benefit, like an unkosher animal to which [the laws of] misappropriation (me'ilah) apply, and similarly with land if one dug out a clod of earth from it, and even while attached there is at least a prohibition; "[it is] for [his] monetary value — he did not say [that]" — [meaning,] that [the slave] himself should be consecrated to be sold. And now [the Gemara] asks well from "no dedicated thing (cherem)," for consecration takes hold of them to become forbidden for benefit, just like one who dedicates other property; and it answers "where he said [it] for [their] monetary value," [meaning] that they should be [consecrated] to be sold, and it is not dealing with one who consecrates using the term cherem. And now it is well [understood] why [the baraita] specifically [mentions] "his Canaanite male slaves and female slaves." And [the Gemara] asks: "The other [baraita] also [refers to a case] where he said [it] for [their] monetary value," and answers: "If so, what are the treasurers doing [here]?" — for the one who consecrated him for his monetary value, he himself should redeem him and he will be his:
